meta.title: Brevard County — the money trail
meta.grand_total_note: The total operating and capital budget the Board of County Commissioners adopted on September 22, 2026, for the year that began October 1 (Resolution No. 26-091).
meta.note: Florida counties count every fund in one total — including reserves (money set aside, not spent this year), money moved between funds, and internal insurance pools — so the total is far larger than what the county spends in a year. Departments and offices below are the July proposed budget — from the county’s budget book (Budget by Agency, p. 22, total $2,386,361,863) and its line-item spreadsheets. The adopted book isn’t posted yet, so the $39.5 million the Board added before adoption is shown as one computed line.

nodes.name: Changes between the July proposal and adoption

nodes.note: A separate government with its own elected School Board. This is the district’s whole FY2026-27 budget as proposed July 28, 2026 — every fund, counting money carried in from last year and money left at year’s end — $58.6 million (3.6%) less than FY2026’s adopted $1,626,355,803. The Board held its final budget hearing September 10, 2026; the adopted book isn’t posted yet (Docket #3). The tax rate proposed is 6.302 mills.

nodes.note: Paid by the 1.5-mill capital tax ($119.3 million), the half-cent school sales tax, and impact fees on new homes. The sales tax is budgeted at $34.2 million, half last year’s $69.4 million, because its renewal is on the November 3 ballot (p. 27) — facts only on this site. By state law the district shares capital tax and sales tax money with charter schools (about 14% of the sales tax).
